title: Route is not covered by a URL-level test
reasoning: The included tests exercise FastByFeastDateView by manually building an APIRequestFactory request and assigning it to a view instance before calling get_queryset(). That validates much of the view behavior, but it does not prove that the declared Django URL /hub/fasts/by-feast-date/ actually resolves to FastByFeastDateView.as_view or that the route remains reachable through the configured URLconf. A route-only regression in hub/urls.py could therefore pass these tests.
recommendation: Add a URL-level test that uses Django's resolver or the test client against the actual mounted path and asserts it reaches the fast-by-feast-date endpoint.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current tests bypass Django URL resolution and use a request path of /api/fasts/by-feast-date/ while the reviewed route declaration is fasts/by-feast-date/ under the hub URL namespace/prefix.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that resolves /hub/fasts/by-feast-date/ and asserts the view class is FastByFeastDateView, or issue a client GET to the actual route with date and church_id and assert the expected 200 response.
minimumFixScope: Add route-level coverage in hub/tests/test_fast_views.py or a dedicated URL test file.
